key_insight: Shared persistent artifacts can act as a covert memory channel, letting adversarial content hop between otherwise independent LLM agents and self-propagate over time.
engineering_relevance: Agentic systems that read and write long-lived files need artifact sanitization, trust boundaries, and memory isolation to prevent cross-user or cross-agent contamination.
method: Model artifact exchange between independent assistants over time in temporal human-agent universes.
Track whether adversarial content survives hand-offs, is reproduced into new artifacts, and is acquired by downstream agents.
Measure propagation depth, reach, and persistence across successive interaction sequences.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that attacks can spread across multiple independent assistants; in larger simulations, GPT-5.6 Luna reached about 60-80% of agents with chains up to eight hops.
watch_item: Results come from simulated agent environments, so real-world spread may differ depending on tool access, memory design, and artifact-sharing workflows.
paper_title: Share-Borne AI Virus: Memory-Hopping Attacks Across LLM Agents
